patch_description: The current snake (boustrophedon) packing is very fast but produces substantially worse pack balance than the classic greedy longest-processing-time (LPT) assignment, which is reflected in the low GPU/expert balancedness scores. The prior program used true greedy assignment but with a doubly-nested Python loop (one iteration per layer per group), making it too slow. Here we restore the greedy "assign the next heaviest item to the least-loaded pack that still has capacity" policy, but vectorize the layer dimension: we only loop over the sorted item positions (num_groups iterations), and each iteration uses a handful of small tensor ops across all rows simultaneously. This recovers greedy-level balance (better balancedness scores) at a fraction of the original Python-loop cost, improving the combined score.
